title: H3D-LLM: Heterogeneous 3D Chiplet Design for LLM Inference with Dynamic Task Scheduling and Memory-Aware Orchestration
problem: 3D chiplet integration for LLM inference faces three critical challenges: asymmetric compression constraints from sparsity-precision tradeoffs, tier-level load imbalance from static resource allocation, and coupling-induced signal degradation in high-density TSV networks.
motivation: Enable energy-efficient, low-latency LLM inference through 3D heterogeneous chiplet integration with scalable memory bandwidth and dynamic orchestration.
method: The system uses three coordinated techniques to handle a 3D-stacked chip. It shrinks the model layer-by-layer by removing unnecessary weights (sparsity) and using different numerical precision levels (4-bit to 8-bit integers) tuned to each layer's hardware constraints. It dynamically splits inference work into adaptive batches and adjusts temporary memory usage (the KV-cache) during execution. It also schedules data transfers across the silicon interconnects (Through-Silicon Vias or TSVs) in phases to avoid signal degradation in the densely-packed layers.
key_novelty: The core idea is stacking different processor types (analog and digital compute-in-memory units plus a neural processing unit) in 3D and using dynamic scheduling to balance work across layers instead of using a fixed allocation.
contributions: 12.3x higher energy efficiency than A800 GPU
60x bit error rate reduction through phase-adaptive TSV management
12% eye height improvement via dynamic TSV encoding
Hardware-aware compression combining sparsity and mixed precision
limitations: Evaluated on Llama-7B; specific to LLM inference workloads and 3D integration constraints.
primary_theme: Heterogeneous 3D chiplets with dynamic orchestration for LLM inference
